findings.title: totalPages is off by one when user_count is a multiple of limit
findings.body: totalPages is computed as Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1. When user_count is an exact multiple of limit (e.g. 50 members and limit 50) this returns 2 instead of 1. The template then renders '1/2', and because showingLast compares currentPage to this wrong totalPages, the 'next' link is not disabled on what is really the last page. Clicking next advances offset to user_count, findMembers requests that offset, the server returns an empty page, and the user is left looking at an empty member list. Use Math.ceil(user_count / limit) (or Math.floor((user_count - 1) / limit) + 1).

findings.title: remove_member deletes the join row directly and leaves groups.user_count stale
findings.body: remove_member removes the membership with group.users.delete(user_id) followed by group.save, instead of using the Group#remove path. The groups.user_count column is a denormalized counter (the .index spec shows it is stored and populated by group.add). Deleting the join record directly bypasses whatever keeps that counter in sync (Group#remove and/or a counter cache / GroupUser callbacks, which delete_all does not trigger), so after removing a member the stored user_count remains too high. The admin groups list and the group header render that stored count, so they will report a wrong member total until it is recomputed. Use Group#remove (or recompute user_count) and cover it with a spec asserting user_count — the current spec only asserts users.count.

findings.title: Group members endpoint now silently truncates to 50 with no pagination on the public page
findings.body: members now always paginates: limit defaults to 50 and the previous behavior (all members for non-automatic groups, up to 200 for automatic groups) is gone. The public group members page (app/assets/javascripts/discourse/templates/group/members.hbs) was not given pagination controls and only iterates `members`, so any group with more than 50 members now silently shows just the first 50 with no way to load the rest. In addition the response changed from a bare array to {members, meta}, which breaks any client of the public /groups/:id/members.json route that still expects an array. Either add pagination to that template or keep returning the full list for this endpoint.

findings.title: add_members splits usernames without stripping whitespace
findings.body: add_members does usernames.split(",") and passes each element straight to User.find_by_username without stripping. If the client ever submits a space-separated list such as "alice, bob", the lookup for " bob" fails and that user is silently not added (the old Group#usernames= setter stripped entries). Strip each element and drop blanks before lookup.

findings.title: Unbounded limit parameter on the public members endpoint
findings.body: members reads the caller-supplied limit with no upper bound: (params[:limit] || 50).to_i. This is a public (non-admin) route, so a request with limit=1000000 forces the entire membership set to be loaded and serialized in one response. Clamp limit to a sane maximum (e.g. the page size) before applying it.

findings.title: remove_member test uses PUT although the route is DELETE
findings.body: The 'cannot remove members from automatic groups' example issues xhr :put, :remove_member, but config/routes.rb maps remove_member to DELETE. Controller specs bypass routing, so the test passes even though it never exercises the real verb/route the browser uses; a mismatch between the configured route and the action would go undetected. Issue :delete here to match the actual route (the 'is able to remove a member' example already uses :delete).
